focus: Q2: exercise release-update.cjs across vendored-without-tags, offline, prerelease, rename, deletion, binary/generated file, partial/interrupted apply, and rollback scenarios; compare behavior with tests.
answeredQuestions: Q2: Does release-update.cjs behave correctly in real operator scenarios (vendored tree without tags, offline, prereleases, renamed, deleted, binary or generated files, partial or interrupted apply, rollback), and does a test cover each?

label: Abrupt apply termination can leave the exclusive lock behind: apply writes rollback.json before sequential file writes but removes the lock only in finally, while rollback must acquire that lock; the caught-error test does not cover process termination.
Binary detection treats only NUL-containing or invalid-UTF-8 bytes as binary, so valid-UTF-8 NUL-free binary content can enter text merging; the existing binary test covers NUL-containing bytes only.

Generated-file handling recognizes four fixed path patterns; other generated outputs fall back to ordinary customization/conflict classification, and tests cover only leaf-manifest and graph-metadata behavior.

Renames are classified by exact path rather than rename identity; same-unit moves become delete-plus-add and whole-unit moves leave the old unit pending explicit deletion decisions, with no direct rename test.

Offline with a vendored tree that has no local tags fails closed as unknown/blocked, but tests do not cover this combined case; the existing offline case checks directory visibility when a recorded release cannot resolve.
